full_judgment: 4. The defendant appeared and filed written statement. His case is that jote recorded under CS Khatian No. 285 of Mouza Mirpur along with other lands under different Khatians belonged to one Sk. Munshi and Bahar Ali and their names were duly re-corded in the CS Khatian. On amicable partition Sk. Bahar got the suit land along with other lands. There-after Bahar Ali died leaving only son Manik Chand. Manik Chand continued to possess the suit land. The plaintiff Abdul Huq is the son of late Sk. Munsih. While Manik Chand was the owner in possession of the suit plot he sold the suit land along with other lands to one Zainul Abedin Master under registered Kabala dated 6.3.42 corresponding to 22nd Falgun, 1348 BS and made over possession to the purchasers. While said Zainul Abdin Master was possessing the suit land he permanently settled the suit land with the defendant under a registered kabuliyat dated 24.10.1951 corresponding to 6th Kartick, 1358 BS and made over possession of the suit land to this defendant and realised rent from him till the acquisition of the rent receiving interest by the Government. The defendant got his name recorded in all stages of SA and RS operation, mutated his name in the Government Sherista and has been regularly paying rent. The suit plot was once acquired by the Government in LA case No. 15/1955-56 and all notices relating to owner-ship and possession of the suit land were issued to the defendant. The scheme for which this land was acquired was ultimately abandoned by the Government and the suit plot was released in favour of the defendant. The defendant is in possession of the suit land althrough.
